text:
lucas: Hey team, vendor LisbonCompute Lda invoiced us for a SaaS subscription and charged 23% PT VAT. Their VAT ID looks valid but their note says they9re using OSS for cross-border digital services. Invoice: 
``
Vendor: LisbonCompute Lda
VAT: PT123456789
Invoice: LC-2026-701
Service: 12 months model inference credits
Net: 10,000 EUR
VAT 23%: 2,300 EUR
Total: 12,300 EUR
```
Link: https://vendors.example.com/lisboncompute/invoice/LC-2026-701

isabel: If they9re using the OSS (One-Stop Shop) to remit VAT for B2C sales, fine. But for B2B sales we should be reverse-charged when we provide our EU VAT ID. Do we have a Portugal VAT match or is this cross-border?

ap-bot: (automated) Redwood VAT IDs: EU123456789 (validated). Vendor onboarding: VAT ID PT123456789 validated via VIES. Invoice flagged: vendor_marked_oss:true.

lucas: This is billed to Redwood EU entity with EU VAT ID provided on the PO. Vendor still charged VAT and noted "OSS return applied". They claim their platform treats all sales as B2C by default.

tax-ops: Quick read: If supply is B2B and buyer provides a valid VAT ID, supplier should issue an invoice without VAT and apply reverse charge. OSS is for sellers to remit VAT on B2C supplies across the EU; it does not justify charging VAT on a B2B sale when buyer is VAT registered. Ask vendor to reissue invoice net of VAT and reference reverse charge (Article 196) and include our VAT ID.

isabel: Operationally AP asks: can we pay now and then recover VAT later if they correct? Prefer not. Holding VAT in suspense seems messy for a subscription.

legal: If vendor insists they9re allowed to charge VAT because of platform constraints, request formal statement and OSS filing evidence for the period. Also get indemnity for any future tax exposure. But we9d rather get a corrected invoice.

lucas: Draft reply: "Thanks. Our purchase was B2B; we supplied our EU VAT ID. Please reissue invoice net of PT VAT with 'reverse charge' and our VAT ID. If your platform defaults to OSS/B2C, please provide OSS reconciliation showing this invoice and an explanation. Until resolved we will not gross-up taxes or accept VAT charged."

tax-ops: That works. If they push for gross-up, escalate to tax counsel. Note: OSS filings are irreversible for the seller after filing period, so insist on corrected docs quickly.

lucas: Sending now and CCing legal & AP. Will update when vendor replies.
